answer_key.title: IKEEXT Remote Service DLL Hijack
answer_key.description: This dataset represents adversaries copying a file remotely to replace a file which is executed by a service that is vulnerable to DLL hijack. This dataset includes

verdict.assessment: An operator used PowerShell to create and deploy a malicious DLL (wlbsctrl.dll) to WORKSTATION6 via admin shares, then manipulated the IKEEXT service to load it. Simultaneously, the domain controller was used to request directory replication rights, indicating a DCSync attack to extract credentials.

findings.name: DLL
findings.behavior: User pgustavo executed PowerShell commands to copy a malicious DLL (wlbsctrl.dll) from WORKSTATION5 to WORKSTATION6's System32 directory via UNC path, then stopped and restarted the IKEEXT service to load the DLL.
findings.reasoning: The operator placed a malicious DLL (wlbsctrl.dll) into the System32 directory of a remote host and then restarted the IKEEXT service to force it to load the attacker-controlled DLL, achieving execution through DLL hijacking. This is DLL hijacking rather than lateral movement because the objective is to execute code via service restart, not merely to access a remote share.

findings.name: DCSync
findings.behavior: The domain controller (MORDORDC$) accessed the domain root object with DS-Replication-Get-Changes extended rights, enabling credential extraction via DCSync.
findings.reasoning: The event shows MORDORDC$ accessing the domain root object with DS-Replication-Get-Changes extended rights (AccessMask 0x100 with the specific GUID in Properties), which is the mechanism used in DCSync attacks to extract credentials by simulating domain controller replication. This is the direct abuse of the replication API that defines T1003.006.

findings.name: Command Obfuscation
findings.behavior: PowerShell on WORKSTATION5 created a binary file (wlbsctrl.dll) from byte array data using Set-Content, establishing the payload for service-based code execution.
findings.reasoning: PowerShell decoded a byte array (77, 90, 144, 0...) representing a binary PE file and wrote it to disk as wlbsctrl.dll. This is payload staging via obfuscated file creation—the binary was encoded as decimal bytes to evade detection during transit/storage, then materialized as an executable DLL for service-based execution. This is not C2 encoding (T1132) but rather preparation of a malicious artifact through obfuscation.
